units.source: As you help {#1}Otherguy{/#1} get his boot out of the mud, {#2}Hunter{/#2} comes out of the bushes with what must be nearly a dozen rabbits strung together. He sets them down and starts to untie them. The little bunnies - eyes wide, horrified in the end - all look quite tasty. The hunter grabs one by its neck and twists its body in a circle before pushing all its guts out in one swift motion. He repeats this process until every rabbit has been slaughtered. As he wipes his hand on {#3}Otherguy{/#3}'s cloak, the hunter points to the mound of emptied bunnies at his feet.
units.zh: 你正帮{#1}另一名弟兄{/#1}把靴子从泥里拔出来，{#2}猎人{/#2}便从灌木中钻了出来，手里提着一串兔子，看样子足有近一打。他把兔子放下，开始解绳。小兔子们瞪圆了眼，眼中还留着惊恐，不过看起来都很可口。猎人揪住一只兔子的脖子，将它的身体转了一圈，随即利落地挤出全部内脏。他如此重复，直到每只兔子都处理完毕。猎人一边在{#3}另一名弟兄{/#3}的斗篷上擦手，一边指着脚边那堆掏空了肚子的兔子。

units.source: {#1}{#2}Hunter{/#2} ran on ahead of the party a few hours ago and just now you catch back up to him. He's standing with his foot on a dead deer, its chest punctured by a single arrow. As you approach, he grins and steps off. He says if some of the brothers can help string it up he'll skin it and prep it.{/#1}{#3}Forest birds chitter and chatter above the company's march. The sun winks between the canopy branches, a soft glint that peppers the ground with dots of light. You spot a squirrel resting in one of the sun beams, enjoying the warmth as it gnaws on an acorn. It stops, sensing you watching it, and then it suddenly jerks and a fleck of its blood meets your cheek. You wipe it away, turning back to see that the squirrel has been impaled by an arrow, every shrieking death throe quieter than the last as the volume of its life slowly turns down. {#4}Hunter{/#4} suddenly breaks through the bushes with a bow in hand and a grin on his face. The hunter retrieves his kill and throws it in with a litter of others, a long hunter's line around which are tied all manner of critters foe and friend alike.{/#3}
units.zh: {#1}几个小时前，{#2}猎人{/#2}跑到了队伍前方，你现在才追上他。他正站在那里，一只脚踩着死鹿；鹿的胸口只有一支箭。见你走近，他咧嘴一笑，把脚挪开。他说，只要几个弟兄帮忙把鹿吊起来，他就能剥皮处理。{/#1}{#3}战团在林中行进，头顶鸟鸣啁啾。阳光在树冠枝叶间闪烁，在地上洒下点点柔光。你发现一只松鼠待在一束阳光中，一边享受暖意，一边啃着橡果。察觉到你的注视，它停了下来，忽然又猛地一颤，一点鲜血溅上你的脸颊。你抹去血迹，再看时，才发现松鼠已被一支箭贯穿。它临死前声声惨叫逐渐低弱，仿佛生命的音量正一点点被拧小。{#4}猎人{/#4}忽然从灌木中钻出来，手里拿着弓，脸上挂着笑。他收起猎物，把它和其他猎物串在一起；那根长长的猎绳上，系着各色小动物，不分善恶，谁也没能幸免。{/#3}

units.source: {#1}{#2}{#3/}{/#2}{/#1} {#4}While marching through the forest, {#5}Randombrother{/#5} calls out to the company. You look over to see him pointing somewhere beyond a line of brush. Their purpled faces and grey feet sway and turn, the wind sometimes forcing them to grimly face one another. {#6}Randombrother{/#6} notes that they're wearing wood: signs of their crimes. 'Thief,' reads one. 'Whore' another. 'Traitor' the last. Having seen enough, you tell the men to get moving again.{/#4}
units.zh: {#1}{#2}{#3/}{/#2}{/#1}{#4}穿越森林时，{#5}一名弟兄{/#5}朝战团喊了一声。你望过去，见他指着灌木丛后方。走到他身边，你也看清了：三具尸体吊在树上。紫胀的脸和灰白的脚在空中摇晃转动，风偶尔把它们吹得彼此相对，模样阴森。{#6}那名弟兄{/#6}指出，尸体身上还挂着木牌，写明他们的罪名。一块写着‘盗贼’，一块写着‘妓女’，最后一块写着‘叛徒’。你已经看够了，便让众人继续上路。{/#4}

units.source: The forest offers no relief, no little road or sidepath for you to travel down. It is thick and unrelenting and does not seem to want you there. You soon find that it did not want someone else, either: a corpse is found tied up in a thorn bush, legs crooked, arms bent, all rather finagled to to their supposed purpose. The mouth rests agape with the eyes drawn slim in some sort of final frustration. {#1}Randombrother{/#1} catches up to you, looks the body up and down, then nods.
units.zh: 森林不给你片刻喘息，连一条小路或岔道也不肯留。林木密密层层，似乎根本不欢迎你。很快，你发现它也不曾欢迎另一个人：一具尸体被绑在荆棘丛中，双腿歪折，两臂弯曲，仿佛被人费力摆成了某种姿势。死者嘴巴张着，双眼眯成细缝，似乎还含着临死前的不甘。{#1}一名弟兄{/#1}赶上来，上下打量尸体，随后点了点头。

provenance.method: Independent complete-unit English/Chinese translation and review, including every displayed branch.

units.source: You stare up at the forest canopy, watching what angles the lightbeams are coming in at. While getting your bearings, {#1}Randombrother{/#1} comes by looking rather distraught.
units.zh: 你仰望树冠，观察光束从哪些角度照进来，正借此辨认方向，{#1}一名弟兄{/#1}走了过来，神情十分不安。

units.source: You shake your head in disbelief. Having seen enough, and having no answer for such questions, you quickly usher the rest of the men away from the clearing and get back to marching.
units.zh: 你难以置信地摇了摇头。已经看够了，也无法回答那些问题，你赶紧催着其余弟兄离开空地，继续行军。

units.source: {#1}You stop at a creekbed to wash yourself and get something of a drink, but before you take the first sip {#2}Randombrother{/#2} grabs your shoulder. He points upriver. A woman's body is face down in the water, her long hair twisting rather lively to the ripples. You thank the sellsword for saving you from any disease the dead press onto the world.{/#1}
units.zh: {#1}你在溪边停下，想洗把脸，再喝点水。然而，第一口水还没送进嘴里，{#2}一名弟兄{/#2}便抓住了你的肩膀，指向上游。一个女人的尸体面朝下浮在水中，长发随着涟漪扭动，竟有几分鲜活。你向这位佣兵道谢，幸亏他让你避开了死人可能带来的疫病。{/#1}

provenance.method: Independent complete-unit English/Chinese translation and review, including every displayed branch.

units.source: The tree canopy is thick and twisting. Whatever light there is above can barely come through, braids of shadow encompassing your men as they march. But further on ahead you see a pillar of light gleaming into the forest. Naturally, someone else saw it first. And it was the last thing they saw.
units.zh: 树冠浓密，枝条纠缠，上方的光几乎透不下来。弟兄们向前行进，交错的阴影将他们笼罩。可再往前，你看见一道光柱照进森林。显然，早有人先看见了它。那也是那人看见的最后景象。

provenance.method: Independent complete-unit English/Chinese translation and review, including every displayed branch.

units.source: {#1}A dead body. Rather, what should be a body. The chest is open and the viscera laid out in all directions, grey and sagging and soft. You can't tell if it was a man or woman, only that it had to have been an adult cut down to much smaller sizes. What creature could have done this work is beyond you, though {#2}Randombrother{/#2} suggests maybe it was the deed of a very determined man.{/#1}{#3}You find the body of a woman with its back resting against a tree. There is a knife in her chest, the wound so quickly fatal that she appears to have died while in some motion of life. Above her, another woman swings from a branch. Red are her clothes. The body's head tilts forward as though to stare at her crime, and the rope that hangs her there groans to a muted wind.{/#3}{#4}You come across some scene of battle. Men, armor, weapons, not a single one of them useable. The dead got that way through some sheer form of brutality you do not wish to learn. Footprints in the earth suggest something big had come through, leaving behind a wake of ruin and calamity, and no urge on your part to follow where those steps go.{/#4}{#5}Marching along, you find a dead man with a few broken arrows in his back. More puncture wounds where his killer managed to retrieve his ammunition in one piece. The man was carrying a love letter, its destination a woman that had, apparently, already been spoken for. Ah, romance.{/#5}
units.zh: {#1}一具尸体。或者说，一堆本该是尸体的东西。胸膛被剖开，灰白、松软的内脏拖得到处都是。你分不清死者是男是女，只能看出那原本应是个成年人，如今却被切成了许多小块。你想不出什么怪物能干出这种事，不过{#2}一名弟兄{/#2}觉得，也可能是某个下了狠心的人干的。{/#1}{#3}你发现一个女人的尸体，背靠着树。她胸口插着一把刀，那一击致命得太快，以至于她还保持着生前动作做到一半的姿态。她上方的枝头吊着另一个女人，身上穿着红衣。吊死者垂着头，仿佛正凝视自己的罪行；微风无声地吹过，悬着她的绳索却呻吟作响。{/#3}{#4}你来到一处战斗遗址。尸体、护甲、武器，已经没有一样能派上用场。这里的人死于一种你不愿了解的骇人暴行。地上的足迹表明，某个庞然大物曾经过此地，身后只留下毁灭与灾难。你丝毫不想沿着脚印追过去。{/#4}{#5}行进途中，你发现一名死者，背上插着几支断箭。此外还有更多贯穿伤，是凶手将完好的箭拔走后留下的。他身上带着一封情书，收信人是个女人——看样子，她早已名花有主。唉，爱情。{/#5}

units.source: He turns to you grinning. His eyes glint white, blinded by old age. A very nice, very expensive looking jeweled ring glistens on one of his bony fingers.

units.source: {#1}You kick the man down. He grunts as though you'd just punted a pregnant boar. Turning over and clutching his stomach, he asks why, but you only kick him again to get him on his back. From there you easily rob him of the jeweled ring and make your leave.{/#1}{#2}The man smacks his old-man lips, that disgusting, crackling dry-mouth noise. In return, you rear back and throw a punch right into his stomach. Not seeing it coming, the elder eats it in full, blowing the air out of his lungs and bowling over. As he gasps for breath, you relieve him of the ring and leave.{/#2}
units.zh: {#1}你一脚把老人踢倒。他闷哼一声，那动静活像你刚踢中了一头怀孕的母猪。他翻过身，捂着肚子问你为什么，你却又踢了一脚，让他仰面朝天。接着，你轻轻松松抢走他的宝石戒指，扬长而去。{/#1}{#2}老人咂了咂干瘪的嘴唇，发出那种老人嘴干时令人厌烦的细碎响声。你则往后一蓄力，一拳直捣他的腹部。他看不见这一拳，结结实实挨了个正着，肺里的气都被打了出来，弯腰倒下。趁他喘不过气，你摘走戒指，转身离开。{/#2}

He rolls over and espouses some wisdom about violence between men. You boot him in the chest and tell him to shut up. The ring comes free of his finger with ease and you make your leave.
units.zh: 你一脚踢开老人的手杖，他踉跄着栽倒在地，瘦骨嶙峋的身子像破败的棚屋一样塌了下去。他翻过身，开始讲人与人不该动武之类的道理。你一脚踹在他胸口，让他闭嘴。戒指轻而易举地从他指头上脱了下来，你随即离去。

provenance.method: Independent complete-unit English/Chinese translation and review, including every displayed branch.

units.source: {#1}Randombrother{/#1} comes to you rubbing his jaw. He says he almost broke his teeth on a bit of bread. Apparently he found the piece at the bottom of a food crate and it appears to have been sitting there for some time. You take a sword to the loaf, chopping it in two as a few brothers cheer with sarcastic bravado. Taking up the halved bread, you show the men the insides: a dark core of black. That's what your stomach will look like if you eat this, you say before throwing the bread into the bushes where you can hear it tumbling like a heavy stone.
units.zh: {#1}一名弟兄{/#1}揉着下巴走过来，说一块面包差点把他的牙硌断。他是在食品箱底找到那块面包的，看起来已经放了很久。你拿剑把面包劈成两半，几个弟兄故作豪迈地为你喝彩，语带讥讽。你拿起半块面包，让众人看里面：面包芯已经黑成一团。‘吃了它，你们肚子里就会变成这样。’说完，你把面包扔进灌木丛，听它像块沉石一样一路滚落。

units.source: {#1}Randombrother{/#1} yelps and leaps up off the log he was sitting on. You walk over to see he's thrown a fish by the wayside and he can't stop pointing at it. While he warns you to not go near it, you decide to go near it. Apparently a water-spider had birthed a clutch of eggs inside the fish's abdomen. You now stare at the little spiderlings bubbling forth in a cloud of scuttling legs and bodies.
units.zh: {#1}一名弟兄{/#1}尖叫一声，从坐着的圆木上跳了起来。你走近一看，他把一条鱼扔在路边，不停指着它。他警告你别靠近，你却偏要过去看看。原来有只水蜘蛛在鱼腹中产了一窝卵。你眼睁睁看着小蜘蛛不断涌出，密密麻麻的身体和细腿乱作一团。

units.source: Childish giggling wakes you from a nap. You rise up to see that some of the food is gone and the only evidence as to where it departed is a field of still moving tall grass. Thinking fast, you take up a sword and follow its trail. Unfortunately, it isn't long before you are lost in the midst of enormous stalks of green that pedal against your face with every rush of wind. The giggling doesn't stop, however, and you hear the pitter-patter of footsteps cross behind you and then in front. A voice speaks, sounding like a child deep in a well.
units.zh: 孩童般的咯咯笑声把你从小睡中惊醒。你起身发现少了些食物，唯一的去向线索，是一片还在晃动的高草。你立刻抓起剑，循迹追去。可没过多久，就迷失在高大的绿草之间；每阵风掠过，草茎都不停拍打你的脸。笑声却没有停，你听见细碎的脚步先从身后跑过，又转到前方。一个声音响起，听起来像是深井里的孩子。

If an armored brute gets past this pointy end here then yer probably proper farked so don't let that happen.{#3/}{#4/}Finally, there's the axe. Just pretend the other man is a tree and cleave it so. units.source: {#1}{#2}{#3}{#4/}{/#3}{/#2} {#5}The swamp clutches at your every step, so wanting you to stay it is. While your boots sink into the mire, {#6}Someguy{/#6} turns and suddenly heaves, adding his breakfast to the bog. You turn to see another brother in the distance double over, loosing from his mouth a great spew that has you choking back some vomit yourself. The {#7}Companyname{/#7} express their collective discomfort as more men wretch and gag. This truly is no place for man to be.{/#5}{#8}While teeming with disgusting forms of life, the swamp actually smells of noxious death. Seemingly toxic steam undulates off the bog's still currents. It burns your eyes and throat and poisons all your foods with ill-tastes. What foul things would dare live here? You see toads and snakes and critters that certainly had the devil's touch in their birthing. The {#9}Companyname{/#9} are uniformly falling sick in this damned place. Only the strong may have the gut to bear it, everyone else is already heaving and seeing things which are not there.{/#8}{/#1}
units.zh: {#1}{#2}{#3}{#4/}{/#3}{/#2}{#5}每迈一步，沼泽都死死拽住你的脚，仿佛一心想把你留在这里。你的靴子陷进泥里时，{#6}一名弟兄{/#6}突然转身呕吐，把早饭全倒进了沼泽。你回头看见远处另一个弟兄也弯下腰，嘴里喷出一大摊秽物，害得你自己都差点吐出来。越来越多的人干呕作呕，{#7}战团名{/#7}的众人无不叫苦。这地方真不是人该待的。{/#5}{#8}沼泽里明明挤满了恶心的活物，闻起来却是有毒的死亡气息。仿佛带毒的蒸汽从滞缓的水流中翻涌升起，灼痛眼睛和喉咙，让所有食物都染上怪味。什么污秽之物才敢住在这里？你看见蟾蜍、蛇，还有些小东西，一看就是出生时遭过魔鬼染指。{#9}战团名{/#9}的弟兄们在这鬼地方纷纷病倒。或许只有身强体壮的人还能忍受，其余人已经吐个不停，眼前甚至出现了幻觉。{/#8}{/#1}

units.source: {#1}{#2}{#3}{#4/}{/#3}{/#2} {#5}The bow isn't quite legendary, but it is quite good. It's light in the grip, easily spun from side to side with the air whistling as it whirls. You test the draw. A strong man will be required to wield it that is for sure. When you loose an arrow, the shaft travels unbelievably straight and the shot almost seems to aim itself. A brilliant weapon if you ever saw one!{/#5}{#6}The bow was constructed with a mix of woods whose names you do not know. Colors of this tree and that spiral through the curve of the weapon, looking arboreally damascened. Testing the draw, the string proves itself mighty. You're no marksman, but when you loose an arrow it almost seems to guide itself to its target. A terrific weapon, if for no other reason it made you look better than you really are. You congratulate the bowyer.{/#6}{/#1}
units.zh: {#1}{#2}{#3}{#4/}{/#3}{/#2}{#5}这把弓还称不上传奇，但确实精良。握在手里很轻，左右转动也十分灵便，挥动间带起阵阵风声。你试了试拉弦，毫无疑问，得有把子力气的人才能驾驭它。箭一离弦，便直得不可思议，仿佛会自己瞄准。你若曾见过真正的好兵器，这绝对算一件！{/#5}{#6}这把弓混用了几种你叫不上名的木材。不同木料的颜色沿着弓身的曲线交错盘旋，宛如木制的大马士革纹。你试着拉弦，弓力果然强劲。你算不上神射手，可射出的箭却像会自己寻找目标。光凭它能让你的箭术看起来远胜真实水平，就足以称得上是件好兵器。你向制弓匠表示赞赏。{/#6}{/#1}

units.source: Obviously, this isn't an ordinary sight for you so, curious, you call out to the weary travelers. Words barely leave your lips before the entire line of men stops in an instant and bolts upright. Their cloaks unravel and droop from their heads, and their tomes and sticks and religious imports fall aside in a uniform clatter. The men look around, wide eyes more alive than ever. One screams. Then another. And soon they are all screaming, and some crumple to the ground, clutching their ears as though to silence the horrid howls their mouths had to give, while others wheel in circles, arms out, begging for answers.
units.zh: 这显然不是你平日常见的景象。出于好奇，你朝那些疲惫的旅人喊了一声。话音刚出口，整列人便同时停下，猛地挺直身子。他们头上的斗篷散开滑落，书册、手杖和宗教物件齐齐掉在一旁，哗啦作响。众人瞪大眼睛四下张望，那双眼从未显得如此鲜活。一个人尖叫起来，接着又是一个，很快人人都在尖叫。有些人瘫倒在地，紧捂双耳，仿佛想堵住自己嘴里发出的骇人嚎叫；另一些人张着双臂原地转圈，拼命追问究竟发生了什么。

units.source: Your mere utterance has seemingly broken a spell that was so long over their heads it had brought them here, impoverished, hungry, and insane. Step by step, they were governed by a malicious higher power, and step by step they felt the control in their lives slip away, and with it the sanity all men require to be themselves. Unfortunately, you can hardly ask them what or who did this to them, for some fall over dead while others make naked sprints into the forest.
units.zh: 你不过喊了一声，似乎就打破了某种长久笼罩着他们的法术。那法术驱使他们来到这里，使他们一贫如洗、饥肠辘辘、精神失常。一路上，他们受某种邪恶的强大力量操纵，一步步失去对自身命运的掌控，也逐渐失去了维系自我的理智。不幸的是，你几乎没法问清是谁或什么东西害了他们：有些人已经倒地而死，另一些人则赤身裸体地狂奔进森林。

units.source: A curious sight such as this begs questioning, but the second a word leaves your lips the entire troop of religious men bolt upright, the sudden shuffle of clothes and gear clattering in such uniformity it as if a door was slammed shut. The men drop their things and begin screaming. It is a raspy chorus. They all begin to collapse, either buckling on bony knees or clutching their stomachs in pained hunger.
units.zh: 这样的奇景自然让人想问个究竟。然而，你才说出一个字，整支信徒队伍便猛地挺直身子。衣物和装备骤然响成一片，整齐得像一扇门砰然关上。众人丢下东西，开始尖叫，汇成一阵沙哑的合唱。随后，他们纷纷倒下，有的瘦骨嶙峋的膝盖一软，有的因饥饿的剧痛而捂住肚子。

provenance.method: Independent complete-unit English/Chinese translation and review, including every displayed branch.

units.source: You won't ever get an answer for a minute later every single man is dead, looking no better than corpses having recently been thawed out of the mountains. The spell must have forcibly piloted their pilgrimage here, straining the human body while keeping it alive by the mere strand of ethereal malevolence. Although they are all dead, you do not regret freeing them of such a horrid curse.
units.zh: 你再也得不到答案了。一分钟后，所有人都已死去，看起来跟刚从山中解冻的尸体没有两样。那法术一定强行操纵着他们朝圣至此，一面榨干他们的躯体，一面又靠着一缕幽冥恶意吊住性命。虽然他们都死了，你仍不后悔让他们摆脱如此可怕的诅咒。

units.source: {#1}{#2}{#3/}{/#2}{/#1} {#4}Walking, running, fighting, fucking, all good for a man's heart. The time spent traveling the land has improved the vitality and vigor of the men. You even caught one of the cheekier mercenaries flexing into pondwater, admiring his own reflection like some smirkin' wench.{/#4}
units.zh: {#1}{#2}{#3/}{/#2}{/#1}{#4}走路、奔跑、打架、上床，全都有益身心。一路走南闯北，弟兄们的体魄和精力都见长了。你甚至撞见一个厚脸皮的佣兵，对着池水鼓起肌肉，欣赏自己的倒影，活像个抿嘴偷笑的姑娘。{/#4}

units.source: All this running about the land has increased the stamina of the men. One runs in place, holding a finger to his neck. He remarks that his heart rate isn't going up at all. Another brother remarks that the guy doesn't even know how to count. The running man pauses.
units.zh: 四处奔走让弟兄们的耐力提高了。一个人原地跑着，把手指按在颈侧，说自己的心跳一点也没变快。另一个弟兄说，他连数都不会数。跑步的人停了下来。

units.source: {#1}{#2}{#3/}{/#2}{/#1} {#4}You step back and let the man take flight. He wraps his face in the scarf and sits into the seat of his machine. With a few long breaths, he pedals it forward. It promptly falls over the edge. The man is hurled through the leather wings like some sort of screaming bat. He spins through the device as it explodes down the rockwall in a torrent of wood and poor design. A moment later, you hear the faint din of his final landing spots. Spectacular!{/#4}
units.zh: {#1}{#2}{#3/}{/#2}{/#1}{#4}你退后几步，让那人起飞。他用围巾裹住脸，坐进机器的座椅，深呼吸几次，便踩动踏板向前冲去。机器立刻翻下悬崖。那人被甩穿了皮革机翼，活像一只尖叫的蝙蝠。他在装置中翻滚，机器沿着岩壁四分五裂，化作一阵由木头和拙劣设计组成的瀑布。片刻后，崖下远远传来几声轻响，那便是他的最终归宿。真是壮观！{/#4}

provenance.method: Independent complete-unit English/Chinese translation and review, including every displayed branch.

units.source: The man pushes his machine off the edge, hopping into its seat at the last moment. They both tip over the precipice and there's a brief scream. But, against all odds, the man quickly reappears! His contraption flutters from side to side like some drunken butterfly, but he's in the air nonetheless.
units.zh: 那人把机器推下崖边，最后一刻才跳上座椅。一人一机翻下悬崖，传来短促的尖叫。然而，出乎所有人的意料，他很快又出现了！那装置像只醉醺醺的蝴蝶，左摇右摆地扑腾着，可无论如何，他确实飞起来了。

provenance.method: Independent complete-unit English/Chinese translation and review, including every displayed branch.

units.source: The machine totters and slowly starts to lose altitude. With the man pedaling harder to compensate, the spokes begin to break and a moment later the whole thing busts apart and you can only watch as the haggard scientist plummets to his doom. The falcon simply squats on the cliff face and watches its enemy die.
units.zh: 机器摇摇晃晃，开始慢慢下降。为了稳住高度，那人拼命加快踩踏，轮辐却开始断裂。片刻后，整个装置彻底散架，你只能眼看着那位形容枯槁的学者坠向死亡。那只猎隼只是蹲在崖壁上，看着自己的敌人死去。

provenance.method: Independent complete-unit English/Chinese translation and review, including every displayed branch.

units.source: Against better judgment, you let the man fly. He bundles his face in the scarf as though that'll save him of the soon to come hard landing. With a deep breath, he pushes his contraption off the edge and leaps in at the last moment as though he were joining his lover in a romantic suicide. The man and machine quickly disappear. You start to laugh when suddenly the man reappears. He's furiously pedaling his machine, the wings flapping hard. He sails around, looping this way and that, slowly getting higher and higher.
units.zh: 尽管觉得不妙，你还是让那人试飞。他拿围巾裹住脸，仿佛这样就能躲过即将到来的猛烈撞击。深吸一口气后，他把装置推下崖边，最后一刻才跳进去，活像要追随爱人浪漫殉情。一人一机迅速消失在视野中。你刚要发笑，那人竟又出现了。他拼命踩着踏板，机翼奋力扑动，载着他盘旋来回，越飞越高。

provenance.method: Independent complete-unit English/Chinese translation and review, including every displayed branch.

units.source: That's the last you see or hear of him.
units.zh: 此后，你再也没有见过他，也没有听过他的消息。

provenance.method: Independent complete-unit English/Chinese translation and review, including every displayed branch.

units.source: The man pushes the machine off the edge and hops into the seat just as it totters over the edge. Screaming, the man climbs back up the contraption as it falls away. He leaps off the last tip of its poorly constructed wooden frame, propelling himself back to the precipice where he hangs on for dear life. You sprint over and drag him back up. His machine smashes into the ground far below, a soft din of predetermined destruction. Brushing himself off, the man nods at you.
units.zh: 那人把机器推向悬崖，在它摇晃着翻下去时跳上座椅。随着装置下坠，他尖叫着沿机器往上爬，从那粗制滥造的木架最末端奋力跃起，扑回崖边，死死抓住边缘。你冲过去，把他拖了上来。远在下方，他的机器砸碎在地，传来一阵轻响，为那注定的毁灭画上句号。那人掸去身上的尘土，朝你点了点头。

provenance.method: Independent complete-unit English/Chinese translation and review, including every displayed branch.

units.source: The way you see it, that went as well as it could have. The men are mightily entertained anyway.
units.zh: 在你看来，事情能有这样的结局，已经算最好不过了。无论如何，弟兄们看得十分开心。

units.source: You eye a traveler in the distance bobbing forth, slouched and crooning like a wingless gargoyle. His walking stick bobs and prods in front of him and even far away you hear the snicker and snacker of stones being tapped. You give an order for your men to hold and wait, letting the stranger come to you.
units.zh: 你看见远处有个旅人摇摇晃晃地走来，佝偻着身子，低声哼着，活像一只没翅膀的滴水兽。他的手杖在前方起落探路，隔着老远，你都能听见杖尖敲击石子的细碎声响。你命令弟兄们停下等候，让那陌生人自己走过来。

provenance.method: Independent complete-unit English/Chinese translation and review, including every displayed branch.

units.source: When he finally nears, he looks up. At first, his nose is all that you see, the rest of him hidden in a cloak. He sniffs gingerly like a blind mole come across a bizarre impasse. Just as you begin to ask if the man is alright, he throws the cloak back, revealing himself. That which faces you is a tired figure. Hobbled. Sleepless days pinch creases about his eyes. Reddened cheeks spread as he smiles. He asks if he might stay with your party for a time.
units.zh: 终于走近时，他抬起了头。起初，你只能看见他的鼻子，其余地方都藏在斗篷里。他小心地嗅着，像一只失明的鼹鼠遇上了古怪的障碍。你正要问他是否安好，他忽然掀开斗篷，露出真容。面前的人疲惫不堪，步履蹒跚，连日失眠在眼角挤出了深深褶皱。他笑起来，泛红的双颊随之舒展，问能否在你的队伍里暂留一阵。

provenance.method: Independent complete-unit English/Chinese translation and review, including every displayed branch.

units.source: {#1}A traveler hails your party from the roadside. He says he's on his way to {#2}Randomtown{/#2} but that he wouldn't mind a rest. The next question he has is an obvious one: he wonders if it'd be alright to stay with your party for the night.{/#1}{#3}A traveler carrying a cart of personal goods heads your way. You let him approach, holding your hand up to warn him to go no further. He states that he is a simple wanderer and that he's only looking to get to {#4}Randomtown{/#4}. First showing that he is completely unarmed, he asks if maybe he can stay the night with your company.{/#3}{#5}A whistling man ambles down the road, a cheery dog huffing at his side with its tongue aloll. Seeing your troop, he stabs his walking stick into the dirt and tents his hands atop it. Some small talk is made of the weather, notably that rain is in the belly of some oncoming clouds. He asks if mayhaps he could dodge the rain in the company of sellswords. A strange request, not one usually made to men who earn blood money.{/#5}{#6}A man walks the road with a shovel bobbing over one shoulder and a sack of dirt swinging in the other hand. When you inquire as to what he is doing, he says he's just buried his brother and he's on his way back to {#7}Randomtown{/#7}. The sack holds some of the dirt where his kin was laid to rest. Respectable. The man looks weary, as weary as a man who has buried his sibling would understandably be. Perhaps sensing your pitying gaze, he asks if maybe he can stay with your company for a time.{/#6}{#8}You spot a strange man hobbling along the road. He's dressed in a long cloak and he's got a knapsack yoked over one of his shoulders. His eyes stare at the ground until they come to your feet at which point he finally looks up. Seeing your company, the man is surprisingly unalarmed. In fact, he's quite receptive of your presence and asks if maybe he could spend the night with sellswords before continuing his journey to {#9}Randomtown{/#9}.{/#8}{#10}A man with a pitchfork is crossing a field where the crops have failed. His feet scuff up the deadened ground and you see tufts of ash being pitched wind-wise. When he gets to the road, you hail him down and ask where he's coming from. The man is a daytaler only trying to get back home. All the work around here is dried up, literally. Licking his cracked lips, the man wonders if maybe he could stay the night with your company. He certainly looks like he could use some rest, anyway.{/#10}
units.zh: {#1}一名旅人在路边向战团打招呼。他说自己正前往{#2}某座城镇{/#2}，不过也想歇一歇。他接下来想问什么，不难猜到：能否跟着战团过一夜？{/#1}{#3}一名旅人拉着装有随身物品的小车，朝你走来。你让他靠近，随后举手示意他别再向前。他说自己只是个普通流浪者，只想去{#4}某座城镇{/#4}。他先证明自己完全没有带武器，然后问能不能跟战团借宿一晚。{/#3}{#5}一个吹着口哨的人沿路缓行，一条兴高采烈的狗跟在身旁，伸着舌头呼哧喘气。看见队伍，他把手杖插进土里，双手叠在杖顶。闲聊几句天气之后，他特别指出，飘来的云层里蓄满了雨水。他问，能否与佣兵们一道避雨。真是个古怪的请求，毕竟人们通常不会向赚血钱的人提出这种事。{/#5}{#6}一个人沿路走来，肩上的铁铲上下晃动，另一只手提着一袋泥土。你问他在做什么，他说刚埋葬了兄弟，正准备返回{#7}某座城镇{/#7}。袋子里装的是亲人长眠之地的泥土。这份情意值得敬重。他看起来疲惫极了——刚埋葬了手足的人，自然会如此。也许察觉到了你同情的目光，他问能否在战团里暂留一阵。{/#6}{#8}你发现一个古怪的人沿路蹒跚而行。他穿着长斗篷，单肩背着行囊，一直盯着地面，直到看到你的双脚才终于抬头。面对整支战团，他竟毫不慌张，反而相当乐意遇见你们。他问，能否跟佣兵们过一夜，再继续前往{#9}某座城镇{/#9}。{/#8}{#10}一个拿着草叉的人正穿过绝收的田地。双脚蹭过死寂的土地，你看见一撮撮灰烬随风扬起。他走到路上时，你叫住他，问他从哪儿来。那人是个短工，只想回家。这一带已无活可干，连田地也真的干透了。他舔了舔干裂的嘴唇，问能否在战团里过一夜。不管怎么说，他看起来的确需要休息。{/#10}

units.source: A man carrying a bucket of tools crosses paths with your company. The roads seem ill-fit to place one man against a company of sellswords, and this stranger appraises the situation correctly by placing his wares down and putting his hands up.
units.zh: 一个提着工具桶的人与战团迎面相遇。在这种路上，独行旅人面对一整队佣兵，显然处境不妙。陌生人也正确判断了形势，放下东西，举起双手。

units.source: You tell him to calm and ask where he is going. He explains that he is a mason from {#1}Randomtown{/#1}, but that his work there is done. He's only on his way back to his family located on a homestead a good day's walk from where you stand. Looking rather thirsty and tired, the man asks if maybe he could spend the night with your company to help him rest for the coming walk.
units.zh: 你让他放松，问他准备去哪儿。他解释说，自己是从{#1}某座城镇{/#1}来的石匠，那边的活已经干完了，如今只想回家。他的家人在一处农庄，离这里足有一天的路程。看起来又渴又累的石匠问，能不能在战团里过夜，养足精神再走接下来的路。

provenance.method: Independent complete-unit English/Chinese translation and review, including every displayed branch.

units.source: {#1}A figure appears on the horizon, blurred and shimmering in a heat haze. It appears to have paused, no doubt having seen you, too. With little fear, you press the men onward and soon come across a man toting a few bags of this or that. He's sitting down on the ground and doesn't bother getting up when you near. He explains he's been on the road for days and could use a good night's rest. Naturally, he asks if he can spend that rest in the company of your men.{/#1}{#2}You come across a man who is weak and weary. He explains that he has been searching for his lost dog, but that he's just about given up. Before he heads home, he wonders quite loudly if maybe a night's rest in your company could help him find the energy to seek out his mutt for one more day.{/#2}{#3}A man tracked by buzzards is found on the side of the road. He's not hurt or wounded, just exhausted. He asks with a cracking voice if maybe he could spend the night in the company of your men.{/#3}
units.zh: {#1}地平线上出现一个身影，在灼热的空气中模糊摇曳。那身影似乎停了下来，想必也看见了你。你没怎么担心，催着弟兄们继续前进，很快就遇见一个带着几袋杂物的人。他坐在地上，见你靠近也懒得起身。他解释说，自己已经赶了好几天路，很需要好好睡上一夜。顺理成章，他问能否在弟兄们身边歇下。{/#1}{#2}你遇见一个虚弱疲惫的人。他说自己一直在寻找走失的狗，却已经快要放弃了。回家之前，他特意大声念叨：要是能跟着战团休息一晚，说不定就有力气再找那条狗一天了。{/#2}{#3}路边有个人，秃鹫一路尾随着他。他没有受伤，只是累得筋疲力尽。他用沙哑的声音问，能不能跟着弟兄们过一夜。{/#3}

units.source: Anyway, the skull seemed to be looking at me, judging me, saying 'what is it you think yer doing here?' So I got up out of that hole and ran to m'home, my cousin's remains yoked over my shoulders like I'd stolen them. I was bothered. Couldn't sleep. Felt like I was laying over what must've been hundreds of fellers right then, some so old they'd taken shape with rocks of all things. Dead fellers. All the way down. Nothing but dead, all the way down I say! And I didn't know what to do and I suppose it still bothers me now if it ain't obvious.
units.zh: 总之，那颗骷髅头像在盯着我，审判我，问我‘你以为自己在这儿干什么？’于是我爬出那个坑，扛着表亲的遗骨跑回了家，那模样活像是偷来的。我心里不安，睡不着。一躺下，就觉得身下有成百上千个死人，有些死得太久，竟然已经和石头长成一体。全是死人，一直往下都是。我是说，一直往下，除了死人什么也没有！我不知道该怎么办，要是你还没看出来，这事到现在还让我心里发毛。

units.source: But the other day I found them bones washed ashore, and there was a fat bellied fish caught in the ribs. Caged himself there on account of good eats, I guess. I picked that fish up and held it, and my cousin I s'pose, in my hand. T'was limp. Bugeyed as fish are without their watery lids. But then a dog ran by and took it from me. Gobbled it right quick for it knew the nature of its crime, I think. That's where a piece of my cousin ran off to. Dodged the earth on account of the hungry rocks only to be eaten by a squire of a fish that served itself to a righteous dog of all things. So now you know why I don't eat fish no more.
units.zh: 可前几天，我发现那些骨头被冲上了岸，肋骨里卡着条大肚子鱼。我猜它是贪吃，结果把自己困在了里头。我捡起那条鱼，捧在手里——这么说，我表亲也算被捧在手里了。鱼软趴趴的，眼睛鼓着，没了水这个眼皮，鱼都那样。可一条狗跑过来，把它抢走了。那狗飞快地吞了下去，想必也知道自己犯了罪。就这样，我表亲的一部分跟着它跑了。为了躲开那些吃人的石头，他逃离了泥土，却被一条小破鱼吃了；而那鱼居然又给一条自命正义的狗送了餐。现在你知道我为什么再也不吃鱼了。

If any survived, it wasn't enough to carry off those who didn't. I like your men. They is good people. But please do be careful out there. Killing raiders and brigands and the gods know what else isn't the only thing you'll be doing. You kill in a market of competitors, sellsword.
units.zh: 几周前，有两三支和你们一样的队伍在十字路口碰上了。那条路大概是容不下所有人吧，他们便打了起来。即使有人活下来，也不够把死者全都抬走。我喜欢你这些弟兄，都是好人。不过在外头千万小心。你们要杀的，可不光是劫掠者、强盗，还有诸神才知道的那些东西。佣兵，你做的是杀人的买卖，可这行里也有同行抢生意。

units.source: But then yonder comes a footman of the mayor who says don't do that. I asked 'im why not, he said 'because that's the mayor's boy'. My punishment was nothing, but I was warned t'not do it again. I told 'im, I said, 'tell the boy to not steal again!'. And they said they had, and that I was more likely to yield to a command than he and that's t'way it t'was. Farkin' small towns, I swear on m'sack those places are more billy than hill.
units.zh: 可这时候，镇长的一名随从过来说，不许那样做。我问为啥，他说‘因为那是镇长的儿子’。我倒没受罚，只是被警告不许再犯。我就说了，‘那你们倒是叫那小子别再偷东西啊！’他们说已经讲过了，只不过比起那小子，我更可能乖乖听话，所以就这么办。去他娘的小镇，我拿自己的卵蛋发誓，那些地方全是一窝不讲理的乡巴佬。

units.source: Cries whip through the party like the howls of the wind. There is not an enemy in sight so you've no idea what is causing this. You walk the ranks to find {#1}Superstitious{/#1} practically sobbing on the ground. He is clutching his chest with one hand while the other points to the sky, the finger shaking in pointed fear. {#2}Otherguy{/#2} explains that the man saw a great blaze of fire cross by the stars. Apparently this pathetic fool takes it for an omen and, of course, it isn't a good one. Whatever it is, it isn't going to get you where you need to be so you order the men to march.
units.zh: 哭喊声像风嚎一样穿过队伍。四下不见敌人，你完全不知道出了什么事。你沿着队列查看，发现{#1}迷信的弟兄{/#1}几乎瘫在地上抽泣。他一只手捂着胸口，另一只手指向天空，手指因恐惧而颤抖。{#2}另一名弟兄{/#2}解释说，他看见一道巨大的火光划过星空。显然，这个可怜的蠢货把它当成了预兆，当然，还不是什么好兆头。管它是什么，都不能帮你们抵达目的地，于是你下令继续行军。

units.source: Shadows begin to fold in and on themselves in strange ways. You turn around to see the sun darkening, a great rim of black moving over it. Soon there is no sun at all. {#1}Superstitious{/#1} cries out that the end times are coming, but before his wailing can find a grip on the rest of your men, the great shade unveils the sun once more and there is light again as though nothing happened at all. You tell the pathetic fool to get to his feet. You've places to march and tears sure as hell won't get you there.
units.zh: 影子怪异地扭曲、重叠起来。你回头望去，只见太阳渐渐变暗，一大片黑影正遮过去。很快，太阳就完全消失了。{#1}迷信的弟兄{/#1}嚷着末日将至，可还没等他的哭号吓住其他人，那片巨大的阴影便再次让出了太阳，光明重现，仿佛什么也没发生。你叫那个可怜的蠢货站起来。你们还得赶路，掉眼泪可走不到目的地。

units.source: You pass beneath a tree whose branches are occupied by both a black cat and an albino crow. {#1}Superstitious{/#1} cries at the sight of it, saying that this is surely a sign of the end times. Why yes, of course it is. These things are never a sign of good things, right? Yeesh.
units.zh: 你们经过一棵树下，树枝上同时待着一只黑猫和一只白化乌鸦。{#1}迷信的弟兄{/#1}一看就叫了起来，说这肯定是末日将至的征兆。是啊，当然了。这些玩意儿就从来不会预示点好事，对吧？真受不了。

Hands trembling, he throws the head out of his hands. It clatters hollow against the ground, tumbling over onto where the horns should be. The scared man claims that a soothsayer once told him that he would come across a skull such as this.
units.zh: 你们遇到一颗鹿的头骨。起初你没觉得有什么，{#1}迷信的弟兄{/#1}却郑重其事地把它捡了起来。他翻来覆去地看，灰尘无声地从空洞中漏出。他双手颤抖，把头骨丢了出去。头骨落地，发出空洞的碰撞声，翻了个个儿，鹿角本该长着的位置朝向地面。那人吓坏了，声称曾有一位占卜者告诉他，他会遇见这样一颗头骨。

units.source: Marching along, a few of the men take up a game of finding shapes in the clouds. They banter back and forth about dogs and fat women and even of home, but the fun takes a wild turn when {#1}Superstitious{/#1} sees one odd-shaped cloud that brings him to his knees. He cries out that it is a bad omen, this cloud, and that doom will soon be upon the company. Thankfully, the fear does not grip the rest of the company who, instead of trembling, soon start bickering over whether or not the cloud is truly representative of {#2}Randombrother{/#2}'s impressive endowment.
units.zh: 行军途中，几个弟兄玩起了看云猜形状的游戏。他们你一言我一语，说云像狗、像胖女人，甚至像自己的家。可当{#1}迷信的弟兄{/#1}看到一朵形状怪异的云时，事情突然变了味：他跪倒在地，大喊那是凶兆，灾难很快就要降临战团。好在其他人没跟着害怕。他们不但不发抖，反而很快吵了起来，争论那朵云到底像不像{#2}另一名弟兄{/#2}那根傲人的家伙。

units.source: {#1}The numbers are counted up and, alas, you have lost. The gambler asks if you wish to go again.{/#1}{#2}Lost! But maybe if you roll again...{/#2}{#3}You lose! A simple roll of the dice, and simple loss. But this one hurts a lot less than which you've seen on the fields of battle. The gambler asks if you wish to have another go.{/#3}{#4}The gods have shunned you and your silly dice. Losing the game is a minor setback, but your pride costs a little more than twenty-five crowns. Should you roll again?{/#4}{#5}The odds have betrayed you for a measly twenty crowns. Maybe if you roll again you can win them back?{/#5}{#6}You watch your dice tumble, seeing for but a moment the winning numbers before it tilts and falls to another side, revealing a losing total. The gambler laughs and asks if you wish to throw again.{/#6}{#7}Your throw was perfect! How could you lose? He needed just those numbers to win! Shaking your head, you wonder if you should roll again.{/#7}

units.source: You come across a caldera the bottom of which you find a few sheep nuzzling something. As you draw close, you see that there is an enormous hound there, its fur matted with blood, its collar shredded, and its paws wiry where the claws have come apart. It regards you with a growl, but can't maintain it for long as it simply puts its head down with an exhausted huff. The sheep depart and beyond them you find a man leaning against a rock. His chest has been ripped open and whatever killed him did it with such force as to spray his innards all along the rocks. Following the trail, you do find a monstrous Nachzehrer whose throat has been ripped out. {#1}Randombrother{/#1} nods.
units.zh: 你们来到一处火山口，看见底下有几只绵羊，正用鼻子蹭着什么。走近后，你发现那里躺着一头巨犬：皮毛被血粘成一团，项圈已经撕碎，利爪断裂处的脚掌露着丝缕筋肉。它冲你低吼，却没力气坚持多久，只疲惫地呼了口气，把头放了下去。绵羊散开后，你看到后面有个人靠在岩石上，胸膛被撕得大开。杀他的东西力气之大，竟把内脏喷溅得岩石上到处都是。顺着痕迹找去，你果然发现了一头庞大的食尸鬼，喉咙已被咬烂。{#1}一名弟兄{/#1}点了点头。

units.source: You reach out to the hound and it lifts it head to you as though you were another threat. Its eyes peer blackly from a long-matted mane that still drips with blood. The sheep, having seen what carnage this beast has already wrought, bay nervously as they watch you. But you won't be deterred. You put your hand forth, palm supinated, and the weary dog slowly lowers into it. You nod.
units.zh: 你向巨犬伸出手，它抬头看你，仿佛又遇到了一个威胁。它的眼睛从纠结的长鬃间阴沉地望出来，鬃毛仍在滴血。绵羊们见识过这头猛兽造成的惨状，此刻看着你，紧张地咩咩叫。但你没有退缩。你把手伸过去，掌心向上，疲惫的狗慢慢把头放进你的掌中。你点了点头。

units.source: You move to take the hound, but as you crouch down one of the sheep bays and charges, knocking you over. The men laugh and by the time you get to your knees another sheep crushes you from behind to many cheers. Drawing out your sword emits a sharp twang that sends the sheep scurrying. When you look back at the hound its nose is to the dirt and its eyes peerless. It has died and the sheep slowly collect around it bleating and crying out. You sheathe your sword and tell the company to move on.
units.zh: 你想把巨犬带走，可刚蹲下，一只绵羊就叫着冲过来，把你撞翻在地。弟兄们笑起来，你才撑起身跪好，又有一只羊从背后撞倒你，四周响起一片喝彩。你拔出剑，锋刃出鞘的锐响惊得羊群四散。再回头看巨犬时，它的鼻尖已经贴在泥土上，眼中再无神采。它死了，绵羊慢慢围拢过来，咩咩哀叫。你收剑入鞘，叫战团继续前进。

They're tired of eating the same thing over and over. Perhaps this could be remedied in the next town the {#2}Companyname{/#2} visits?{/#1}

units.source: "{#1}{#2}{#3}{#4/}{/#3}{/#2} {#5}Sirs, {#6}Settlement{/#6} to the {#7}Direction{/#7} is in dire need of help and has requested any and all able men, particularly those of the sword selling sort, to come and help.{/#5}{#8}Ah, the {#9}Companyname{/#9}, just the sort I was hunting for. {#10}Settlement{/#10} to the {#11}Direction{/#11} is requesting help with a problem. If you're looking for work, I wager you head that way. And make sure to tell them I sent ya, I get two extra crowns for it.{/#8}{#12}Hey there sword selling sirs, {#13}Settlement{/#13} to the {#14}Direction{/#14} is in need of your services. I suggest you head that way if you're looking for work.{/#12}{#15}Looking for work? You don't march like you got purpose, so let me tell ya that {#16}Settlement{/#16} to the {#17}Direction{/#17} has got some jobs for your lot.{/#15}{#18}Ah, a sellsword without a role in this world? Woe is ye. Well, {#19}Settlement{/#19} not far from here has got something for ya. I suggest you get on to it.{/#18}{#20}I'm here to tell yas that {#21}Settlement{/#21} is looking for workers. Not laborers, mind. I'm speaking to you for a reason. Take your swords and killers there if ya want some proper coin.{/#20}{#22}Hey there, ya should know that {#23}Settlement{/#23} is looking for men of your kind. Find your way there and you may have a new job yet.{/#22}{#24}Looking for work are ye? Then get on to {#25}Settlement{/#25} to the {#26}Direction{/#26}, it's no mystery to no one that they're looking for men like you.{/#24}{/#1}"
units.zh: “{#1}{#2}{#3}{#4/}{/#3}{/#2} {#5}诸位，{#7}那个方向{/#7}的{#6}聚落{/#6}急需帮助，正召集一切能干的人前去，尤其是你们这种以刀剑为生的。{/#5}{#8}啊，{#9}战团名{/#9}，正是我要找的人。{#11}那个方向{/#11}的{#10}聚落{/#10}遇到了麻烦，正在求助。要是你们想找活干，我建议往那边去。记得说是我介绍的，这样我能多拿两枚克朗。{/#8}{#12}喂，各位佣兵老爷，{#14}那个方向{/#14}的{#13}聚落{/#13}需要你们效力。要是你们想找活干，我建议往那边走。{/#12}{#15}找活干呢？看你们走路也没个目标，那我就告诉你们，{#17}那个方向{/#17}的{#16}聚落{/#16}有些活适合你们。{/#15}{#18}啊，一位在这世上无事可做的佣兵？真可怜。好了，离这儿不远的{#19}聚落{/#19}有事要你们办。我建议你们赶紧过去。{/#18}{#20}我来告诉你们，{#21}聚落{/#21}正在找人干活。注意，可不是苦力。我找你们说话是有缘由的。想挣笔像样的钱，就带着你们的刀剑和杀人好手过去。{/#20}{#22}喂，告诉你们一声，{#23}聚落{/#23}正在找你们这种人。赶过去，也许就有新活了。{/#22}{#24}想找活干，是吧？那就去{#26}那个方向{/#26}的{#25}聚落{/#25}。那里在找你们这种人，可是人尽皆知的事。{/#24}{/#1}”

units.source: {#1}{#2}{#3}{#4/}{/#3}{/#2} {#5}As you take stock of the inventory, you can't help but notice {#6}Beggar{/#6} lingering in your peripheral. Sighing, you finally turn to the former beggar and ask what he wants. Like the poorest of the poor he holds a hand out, asking if maybe you could spare a few crowns.{/#5}{#7}With practiced theatrics, {#8}Beggar{/#8} approaches you and lets loose a long tale of troubles and squabbles and empty bottles. The former beggar is down on his luck, apparently, and just needs a few extra crowns to get by.{/#7}{#9}{#10}Otherguy{/#10} tells you that {#11}Beggar{/#11} is going around the camp asking for crowns. Apparently the former beggar just needs a little more, expressing a longwinded sob story to anyone who'll listen. Hearing this news, you go to see the man yourself but before you can even get a word out the man lets loose his long narrative. Finished, he looks you in the eye, trying to gauge whether or not you'll give him something.{/#9}{#12}Apparently {#13}Beggar{/#13} the former beggar needs some help. He's come to you, begging for a few crowns to help him get by. The man looks like he's in a poor state, but he's had plenty of practice of actually being poor so it's hard to tell if he's being honest or not.{/#12}{/#1}
units.zh: {#1}{#2}{#3}{#4/}{/#3}{/#2} {#5}清点库存时，你总能从眼角看见{#6}那个当过乞丐的弟兄{/#6}在旁边晃悠。你叹了口气，终于转身问他想要什么。他像最穷的穷人那样伸出一只手，问你能不能赏几枚克朗。{/#5}{#7}{#8}那个当过乞丐的弟兄{/#8}使出熟练的表演功夫，走到你面前，开始长篇大论地诉说麻烦、争吵和空酒瓶的故事。看来，这位前乞丐最近运气不好，只差几枚克朗就能渡过难关。{/#7}{#9}{#10}另一名弟兄{/#10}告诉你，{#11}那个当过乞丐的家伙{/#11}正在营地里四处要钱。显然，他只差那么一点，对任何肯听的人都要哭诉一大通。听到这消息，你亲自去找他，可还没来得及开口，他就开始滔滔不绝地讲述自己的遭遇。终于说完后，他盯着你的眼睛，试图判断你会不会给他点什么。{/#9}{#12}看来，{#13}那个当过乞丐的弟兄{/#13}需要点帮助。他找上你，乞求几枚克朗，好让自己撑下去。他看起来确实很落魄，可他以前受穷的经验太丰富，你很难判断这回说的是不是真话。{/#12}{/#1}

units.source: {#1}{#2}{#3}{#4/}{/#3}{/#2} {#5}You tell the beggar you'll cross his hands with a sword if he doesn't get back to work. The man shrugs and pretty much does as told. That was easier than expected.{/#5}{#6}The beggar's shoulders sag as you tell him to get back to work. You feel a little bad, but then remember that's how they get ya.{/#6}{/#1}
units.zh: {#1}{#2}{#3}{#4/}{/#3}{/#2} {#5}你告诉乞丐，再不回去干活，你就用剑招呼他伸出来的双手。他耸耸肩，倒也照办了。比预想的容易。{/#5}{#6}你叫乞丐回去干活，他的肩膀垮了下去。你有点过意不去，随即想起，他们就是靠这个让你心软的。{/#6}{/#1}

units.source: {#1}{#2}{#3}{#4/}{/#3}{/#2} {#5}The beggar takes the crowns and with a smile gets right back to work.{/#5}{#6}Tired of his games, you give the beggar a few crowns and tell him to get back to work. He bows and thanks you and, surprisingly, actually gets back to work.{/#6}{/#1}
units.zh: {#1}{#2}{#3}{#4/}{/#3}{/#2} {#5}乞丐拿了钱，笑着立刻回去干活。{/#5}{#6}你厌倦了他的把戏，给了他几枚克朗，叫他回去干活。他鞠躬道谢，而后居然真的回去干活了。{/#6}{/#1}

units.source: "{#1}{#2}{#3}{#4/}{/#3}{/#2} {#5}T'was this big. I swear on me mum! Fish so big that when I yanked it from the waters the whole river dried a foot!{/#5}{#6}The ocean is a beast, aye, and the skies above its master, the winds its leash, and we men the fleas.{/#6}{#7}Lost I was! A summer adrift, the whole boat run through with hunting waters, each wave having taken a sailor for itself until only I remained, aye, aye! Tis the truth! By autumn, I saw land again, and so happy I was to see the trees and the mountains and the birds that dwell above both that I smashed my ship right into the rocks and kissed the sands as debris drifted about me. T'was the happiest day of m'life.{/#7}{#8}Never seen a great white whale before, but a green one? Aye. Wore a coat of moss, a stolen land fur if nothing else. We hunted it down with spears and ol' sailor spirit. Alas, it realized we were on it when {#9}Randomname{/#9} - a man with the finest harpoon aim there is - struck it in the blowhole. I did not know a whale could turn 'round so quickly, but it did, and it made short work of our ship and drowned a number of sailors in a fit of vengenace.{/#8}{#10}I once caught a bass about, yeigh, big. Can you believe that? Alright, it was this big. Okay, maybe this big. Alright I've never caught a bass. Fine! I've never even seen a bass! I just know they're out there! Leave me alone you land lovers! I fish the big seas, dammit! I know nothing of your silly ponds. Except bass, of course, I know about them.{/#10}{/#1}"
units.zh: “{#1}{#2}{#3}{#4/}{/#3}{/#2} {#5}足有这么大！我拿我娘发誓！那鱼大得啊，我把它从水里拽上来，整条河的水位都低了一尺！{/#5}{#6}大海是头野兽，没错。头顶的天空是它的主人，风是拴它的绳索，而我们人类，不过是跳蚤。{/#6}{#7}我迷航了！整个夏天都在漂，凶猛的海水灌满了船，每道浪都带走一个水手，直到只剩我一人，没错，没错！千真万确！到了秋天，我终于又看见陆地。见到树、山，还有飞在它们上头的鸟，我高兴极了，直接把船撞上了礁石。我亲吻着沙滩，船的残骸就在身旁漂浮。那是我一生中最快乐的一天。{/#7}{#8}我从没见过巨大的白鲸，可绿鲸？见过。它披着一层苔藓，简直像从陆地上偷来了一件皮衣。我们拿着长矛，凭着老水手的气魄追猎它。唉，直到{#9}一个同伴{/#9}——那可是掷鱼叉最准的人——击中了它的喷水孔，它才发觉我们正在追它。我从不知道鲸鱼能转身那么快，可它确实做到了。它轻而易举地毁了我们的船，大发雷霆地报复，淹死了好些水手。{/#8}{#10}我曾经抓过一条鲈鱼，大概有，喏，这么大。信不信？好吧，是这么大。行了，也许只有这么大。好吧，我从没抓过鲈鱼。好啦！我甚至都没见过鲈鱼！我只知道这世上有！别缠着我了，你们这些旱鸭子！老子是在大海上捕鱼的！我才不了解你们那些破池塘。当然，鲈鱼除外，我知道鲈鱼。{/#10}{/#1}”

They called it, if I recall, a real problem... -strum strum-...{#1/}{#2/}This beast could only feast on the ladies, but just the virgins oh yeah it had great taste!...-plucky strum-... but obviously that was not, for man or woman, a desired fate!...-sketchy strum, a new one-...{#3/}{#4/}So they hired Sir Galicock, the greatest sword-swinger in the land...-playful strum-...and so he went door to door, and vanquished every virgin a good swordsman can!...-a lingering, sad strum-... and the monster starved to death. units.zh: 你告诉{#1}这名弟兄{/#1}，你不认同他对自己应得薪水的估价。他回敬了几句脏话，音量估计可以算作“很大”。骂完之后，他点了点头。

provenance.method: Independent complete-unit English/Chinese translation and review, including every displayed branch.

units.source: {#1}Bro{/#1} presses for more pay, but you put your foot down.
units.zh: {#1}这名弟兄{/#1}坚持要求加薪，你却坚决不肯。

provenance.method: Independent complete-unit English/Chinese translation and review, including every displayed branch.

units.source: {#1}Bro{/#1} gets disloyal (if his mood is angry and he was neither Loyal nor already Disloyal)
units.zh: {#1}这名弟兄{/#1}获得不忠特性（当心情为愤怒，且原本既没有忠诚也没有不忠特性时）。

provenance.method: Independent complete-unit English/Chinese translation and review, including every displayed branch.

units.source: {#1}Bro{/#1} is no longer loyal (if his mood is angry and he was Loyal)
units.zh: {#1}这名弟兄{/#1}失去忠诚特性（当心情为愤怒，且原本拥有忠诚特性时）。

provenance.method: Independent complete-unit English/Chinese translation and review, including every displayed branch.

units.source: We can't always get what we want. (the event ends)
units.zh: 人不可能事事如愿。（事件结束）

provenance.method: Independent complete-unit English/Chinese translation and review, including every displayed branch.

units.source: {#1}Brother{/#1} growls and throws his arms wide like a man overtaken by a primal rage to shed blood.
units.zh: {#1}这名弟兄{/#1}低吼着张开双臂，仿佛被一股渴望鲜血的原始怒火攫住。

provenance.method: Independent complete-unit English/Chinese translation and review, including every displayed branch.

units.source: {#1}Brother{/#1} spits and runs his hand under his nose. His face scowls and he seems to be talking to himself as others look on.
units.zh: {#1}这名弟兄{/#1}啐了一口，用手擦过鼻子下方。他满脸怒容，像是在自言自语，其他人则在一旁看着。

provenance.method: Independent complete-unit English/Chinese translation and review, including every displayed branch.

units.source: 50% of everyone else, except Pessimists, get a {#1}good mood{/#1}
units.zh: 其余成员中，除拥有悲观特性者外，有50%{#1}心情变好{/#1}。

provenance.method: Independent complete-unit English/Chinese translation and review, including every displayed branch.

units.source: A man to go down fighting with. (the event ends)
units.zh: 这人值得与你并肩战斗至死。（事件结束）

provenance.method: Independent complete-unit English/Chinese translation and review, including every displayed branch.

units.source: "Oh it's horrible! Horrible! Would you look at it? But it's okay, understand? It's perfectly okay. Look at me. Look at me!"
units.zh: “哦，太可怕了！太可怕了！你看见了吗？但没事的，明白吗？完全没事。看着我。看着我！”

provenance.method: Independent complete-unit English/Chinese translation and review, including every displayed branch.

units.source: The woman grabs you and spins you. Her once soft features have hardened into blackened flakes, the top of her head already burnt bald, her teeth falling out of dripping gums. Yet she's still grinning.
units.zh: 女人抓住你，把你扳向她。她曾经柔和的面容已变成一片片焦黑的硬皮，头顶烧得寸发不生，牙齿从不断淌出液体的牙龈中脱落。可她仍在咧嘴笑着。

provenance.method: Independent complete-unit English/Chinese translation and review, including every displayed branch.

units.source: {#1/} {#2}"Rest easy, my love. There is nothing to fear in death."{/#2}
units.zh: {#1/} {#2}“安心长眠吧，我的爱人。死亡没什么可怕的。”{/#2}

provenance.method: Independent complete-unit English/Chinese translation and review, including every displayed branch.

units.source: {#1}{#2}{#3}{#4/}{/#3}{/#2} {#5}Food stocks have run out! Despite the horrors of this world, the {#6}Companyname{/#6} can't be fielding a company of skeletons! You need to get the men food fast before they rightfully leave.{/#5}{#7}Even the most loyal of men is only as good as about five or six missed meals. After that, anyone is apt to leave and get themselves fed. Acquire food - and do it fast before the company falls apart!{/#7}{#8}You've miscalculated the food reserves and placed the {#9}Companyname{/#9} into a unique danger - that of going hungry. Even the deadliest of companies would fall apart in days if it goes unfed and this company will be no different if you don't change things fast!{/#8}{/#1}
units.zh: {#1}{#2}{#3}{#4/}{/#3}{/#2} {#5}食物已经耗尽了！尽管这世界恐怖之物横行，{#6}战团{/#6}也不能派一群饿成骷髅的家伙上阵！你得赶快给弟兄们弄到吃的，否则他们离开也是理所当然。{/#5}{#7}再忠诚的人，顶多也就能忍五六顿饿。再往后，谁都可能离开，自己找饭吃。弄到食物——动作要快，别等战团散伙！{/#7}{#8}你算错了口粮储备，让{#9}战团{/#9}陷入一种特殊的危险：挨饿。再凶悍的队伍，断粮几天也会土崩瓦解；你要是不赶快采取行动，这支战团也不会例外！{/#8}{/#1}

provenance.method: Independent complete-unit English/Chinese translation and review, including every displayed branch.

units.source: I need to get the men something to eat. (the event ends)
units.zh: 我得给弟兄们弄点吃的。（事件结束）

provenance.method: Independent complete-unit English/Chinese translation and review, including every displayed branch.

units.source: Still useful. ({#1}{#2}continue{/#2}{/#1} if you have a Butcher, otherwise the event ends)
units.zh: 还派得上用场。（若有屠夫则{#1}{#2}继续{/#2}{/#1}，否则事件结束）

provenance.method: Independent complete-unit English/Chinese translation and review, including every displayed branch.

units.source: And you're sure this is edible still? (the event ends)
units.zh: 你确定这东西还能吃？（事件结束）

provenance.method: Independent complete-unit English/Chinese translation and review, including every displayed branch.

units.source: {#1}{#2}{#3/}{/#2}{/#1} {#4}A wagon, tipped over. Dead horses by its side. One dead donkey with evidence of having put up a fight. Women. Children. A couple of older men. Most mutilated in a fashion unsuitable for being found by anyone, but you figure your company was probably the best fit to come across such ruin. You've got the stomach for it, for you have created worse. It is the innocence of the dead that turns the gut, though, and in a feeble effort to rectify that moral illness you go ahead and bury the dead. Sadly, nothing of value is found in their remains.{/#4}{#5}Blood in the ditch by the side of the road. Blood all across the road. Blood in the ditch on the other side of the road. Blood up on the canvas of the wagon. Blood in the dead's eyes and blood in their mouth. One poor farmer, deceased, seemingly happened upon by a band of thieves for nothing of value he carried remains in the ruin you've stumbled upon.{/#5}
units.zh: {#1}{#2}{#3/}{/#2}{/#1} {#4}一辆翻倒的货车，旁边是死马。一头死驴身上还有奋力反抗过的痕迹。女人，孩子，几个老人。大多被残害得不堪入目，任谁撞见都难以承受，可你觉得，这样的惨状或许最适合让你们战团遇见。你们承受得住，因为更惨的场面，你们也亲手制造过。但死者的无辜仍让人腹中翻腾。为了稍稍平息良心的不适，你着手埋葬了他们。可惜，遗物里没找到值钱的东西。{/#4}{#5}路边的沟里是血。路上到处是血。另一侧的沟里也是血。货车的篷布上是血。死者眼里是血，嘴里也是血。一个可怜的农夫死在这里，看来撞上了一伙盗贼，因为在你发现的这片狼藉中，他随身带的值钱物品已荡然无存。{/#5}

provenance.method: Independent complete-unit English/Chinese translation and review, including every displayed branch.

units.source: The birds were the first hint: cycling and turning over a distant calamity. You figured whatever they saw was still alive, but by the time you got to it the flock had landed and you stumbled across a dead man leaning up against a sidepost.
units.zh: 最先透露端倪的是飞鸟：它们盘旋翻飞，聚集在远处某场灾祸上方。你原以为它们盯上的东西还活着，可等你赶到，鸟群已经落地，你看到一个死人靠在路旁的木桩上。

provenance.method: Independent complete-unit English/Chinese translation and review, including every displayed branch.

units.source: You try and scare the birds away. The black buzzards only hop a few steps in the opposite direction where they then turn to stare at you. The corpse is fresh, the means to its death a slow one: a few arrows stick out of his side. A rope on his hip suggests he had a purse there. Someone robbed him - twice.
units.zh: 你试着把鸟赶走。黑色的秃鹫只是朝另一边跳了几步，便转身盯着你。尸体还很新鲜，他死得却很缓慢：几支箭插在他的肋侧。腰间的绳子表明，那里原本挂着一个钱袋。他被抢了两次——先是钱，再是命。

provenance.method: Independent complete-unit English/Chinese translation and review, including every displayed branch.

units.source: {#1}You stumble across a few hanged criminals. They swing from a tree by the side of the road, their faces mere impressions beneath the woolsacks over their heads. A few of them show signs of torture: gashes here and there, the glaring muscles turning purple and some already grey. Blood beneath one's feet, suggesting someone had a go at him while he suffocated. Naturally, they have nothing of value so you get back on the road.{/#1}{#2}A goat with a bell cradled in the arms of a dead shepherd. You found the pair by the side of the road. The animal's throat is open, and the man's body has no wounds. Maybe he died of a broken heart. {#3}Randombrother{/#3} rifles through the dead man's pockets and comes up empty handed. You decide to leave the two where they were.{/#2}
units.zh: {#1}你偶然遇到几个被绞死的犯人。他们在路边的树上晃荡，头套着毛布袋，只隐约透出脸的轮廓。有几人身上留着受过酷刑的痕迹：伤口遍布各处，暴露的肌肉变成紫色，有些已泛灰。其中一人脚下有血，说明在他窒息时，还有人对他下了手。他们自然没有什么值钱的东西，你便重新上路。{/#1}{#2}一只挂着铃铛的山羊，蜷在死去牧羊人的怀里。你在路边发现了他们。羊的喉咙被割开，人的身上却没有伤。也许他死于心碎。{#3}一名弟兄{/#3}翻遍死者的口袋，一无所获。你决定让这一人一羊留在原处。{/#2}

provenance.method: Independent complete-unit English/Chinese translation and review, including every displayed branch.

units.source: Two buzzards clasp a string of intestine between the two of them, slowly chomping it down until their beaks clack together. You'd be humored if it weren't for where this meal had come from: a dead child, he or she lying face down on the ground. The back had been torn away, a lurid ribcage glistening in the sun.
units.zh: 两只秃鹫各衔着一段肠子的两头，慢慢吞食，直到鸟喙碰在一起。如果不是因为这顿饭的来源，你也许会觉得好笑：一个死去的孩子伏在地上，分不清男女，后背被撕开，惨不忍睹的胸廓在阳光下泛着光。

provenance.method: Independent complete-unit English/Chinese translation and review, including every displayed branch.

units.source: You scare off the birds - though they are quite reluctant to be scared at all - and then bury the body. Moving back onto the road, you see the two birds squatting over the grave, picking and prodding at the dirt {#1}{#2}{#3}{#4/}{/#3}{/#2} {#5}in some sort of avian angst{/#5}{#6}as if to somehow recreate the process they'd seen but in reverse{/#6}{/#1}. Giving up, they eventually take flight, circling above your band of men for a mile or two before heading elsewhere.
units.zh: 你赶走那些鸟——尽管它们一点也不情愿受你惊吓——然后埋葬了尸体。回到路上时，你看见那两只鸟蹲在坟上，{#1}{#2}{#3}{#4/}{/#3}{/#2} {#5}仿佛在发泄某种鸟类的焦躁{/#5}{#6}仿佛想把刚才看见的过程倒着重做一遍{/#6}{/#1}，不停啄弄泥土。最终它们放弃了，振翅飞起，在队伍头顶盘旋跟随了一两英里，才飞往别处。

provenance.method: Independent complete-unit English/Chinese translation and review, including every displayed branch.

units.source: {#1}The fires crackle and pop as they consume the last of the wagon. {#2}Randombrother{/#2} picks through the blackened mess, but comes up empty handed. A few hands can be found sticking up out of the ash and soot, their forms as equally black. The bodies are completely gone, buried or burned away or buried beneath that which was burned away. Seeing as how there is nothing to salvage, you quickly get the company back on the road.{/#1}{#3}A dead horse. Its rider is across the road, having crawled to his final resting spot. Broken arrows litter the path, the heads of them ripped off and salvaged. The man is missing his scalp, the cap of his head glinting and red. After a quick search you realize there's nothing here to take and decide to move on.{/#3}{#4}You come across a pile of naked bodies by the side of the road. Some of them look ghastly, as though they've been dead for a great long while, though rather fresh blood is in some of their mouths. A few of the corpses carry color in their flesh, but they have what look like bite marks here and there. Preemptive measures were taken, it seems, for every one of them has had his or her neck slashed. Naked as they are, you naturally find nothing but what is natural to nature itself. You move on.{/#4}{#5}You feel as though you are being stared at and stop, quickly turning to the side of the road with a hand on your sword. A head stares back at you with its eyes barely peeping over some grass. {#6}Randombrother{/#6} walks over and picks it up. The face carries the visage of a rather jarring death, being so slackjawed and slanted. You tell the sellsword to put the head down for you've better things to do.{/#5}
units.zh: {#1}火焰噼啪作响，吞噬着货车最后的残片。{#2}一名弟兄{/#2}翻找焦黑的残骸，却一无所获。灰烬和烟尘中伸出几只手，同样黑得如炭。尸身已完全不见，或被掩埋，或被烧毁，或埋在烧毁的残骸之下。既然没什么能捡的，你很快叫战团重新上路。{/#1}{#3}一匹死马。它的骑手倒在路的另一边，那是他爬到的最终归宿。断箭散落在路上，箭头已被拔走回收。那人失去了头皮，头顶一片红亮。匆匆搜查后，你发现这里没什么可拿，便决定继续前进。{/#3}{#4}你在路边遇到一堆赤裸的尸体。有些面目骇人，仿佛已死去很久，嘴里却还带着相当新鲜的血。另一些尸体的皮肉尚有血色，身上却到处是疑似咬痕。看来有人采取了防患未然的措施，因为每具尸体的脖子都被割开了。他们赤身裸体，除了天生长在身上的东西，自然再无其他。你继续前进。{/#4}{#5}你觉得有人在盯着自己，便停下脚步，手按剑柄，迅速转向路边。一颗人头回望着你，双眼刚好露出草丛。{#6}一名弟兄{/#6}走过去，把头捡起来。那张脸下巴松垮、五官歪斜，显然死得极为惨烈。你叫佣兵把头放下，你们还有更要紧的事。{/#5}

provenance.method: Independent complete-unit English/Chinese translation and review, including every displayed branch.

units.source: {#1}{#2}{#3/}{/#2}{/#1} {#4}You find a dead goblin. But it's no ordinary goblin - this is an elder. He or she's showing signs of dying of old age. There's also ceremonial trinkets all about it. This here goblin didn't get here by accident: it died and received a proper burial. Which means only one thing: you're in those damned greenskins' territory.{/#4}
units.zh: {#1}{#2}{#3/}{/#2}{/#1} {#4}你发现一具地精尸体。可这不是普通地精，而是一位长者。无论男女，它看起来都是寿终正寝，周围还摆着各种仪式用的小饰品。这地精出现在这里绝非偶然：它死后得到了正式安葬。这只意味着一件事——你们已踏进那些该死绿皮的领地。{/#4}

provenance.method: Independent complete-unit English/Chinese translation and review, including every displayed branch.

units.source: You come across a dead dog on a hillside. Its tongue hangs out, its eyes almost ready to pop from the skull. A number of darts are sticking out of its fur. {#1}Randombrother{/#1} plucks one and looks at the tallowed tips of metal.
units.zh: 你在山坡上遇到一条死狗。它舌头耷拉在外，眼睛几乎要从眼眶里凸出，皮毛间插着许多吹箭。{#1}一名弟兄{/#1}拔出一支，查看那涂着油脂状物质的金属尖端。

provenance.method: Independent complete-unit English/Chinese translation and review, including every displayed branch.

units.source: A wreath of odd and discolored flowers, weeds, and tree limbs. Amongst them, dozens of large beetles rattle as their shells bump into one another. They seem to be feasting on the sap or other oddity seeping from the vegetative collection. {#1}Randombrother{/#1} wonders aloud.
units.zh: 一个用怪异、变色的花朵、杂草和树枝编成的环。其间几十只大甲虫爬来爬去，甲壳相撞，咔嗒作响。它们似乎正啃食这堆植物中渗出的汁液或其他怪东西。{#1}一名弟兄{/#1}忍不住出声猜测。

provenance.method: Independent complete-unit English/Chinese translation and review, including every displayed branch.

units.source: While marching through the land, you come across a dead orc. He seems almost unhurt, as though you'd stumbled across him sleeping. But when you get a closer look, you spot almost a dozen small darts sticking out of his side. You immediately get a good look at your surroundings, then turn to your men.
units.zh: 行军途中，你们遇到一具兽人尸体。它看起来几乎毫发无损，仿佛只是睡着了。可走近一看，你发现它身侧插着近十几支细小的吹箭。你立刻仔细扫视四周，随后转向弟兄们。

provenance.method: Independent complete-unit English/Chinese translation and review, including every displayed branch.

units.source: {#1}You find a number stones arranged into a circle. In the middle of this oddity is a human skull with its top cut away. Inside the brainpan are a number of what appear to be dice and chicken bones. Such shamanistic designs aren't found by accident - you're in goblin lands.{/#1}{#2}You come across a dead deer ensnared by a horrifying trap. It would have all the markings of an ordinary trap - one that intends to kill via spikes - were it not for the obvious poison tips it came laden with. Poison that is unique to one group only: goblins. Best step carefully from now on.{/#2}
units.zh: {#1}你发现一些石头摆成了一个圆圈。这个古怪阵势中央放着一颗削去顶盖的人类头骨，颅腔里装着一些疑似骰子和鸡骨头的东西。这样的萨满布置不是偶然出现的——你们已来到地精的领地。{/#1}{#2}你遇到一头死鹿，被困在骇人的陷阱里。要不是那些尖刺明显淬了毒，它本该只是个靠尖刺杀死猎物的普通陷阱。而这种毒，只有一类家伙会用：地精。从现在起，最好小心落脚。{/#2}

provenance.method: Independent complete-unit English/Chinese translation and review, including every displayed branch.

units.source: A smoldering fire. Sticks and stones arranged for this or that. One standing armory stocked with blowguns. Curved blades. And one dead wolf pup with a leash around its neck. Having observed this evidence, you quickly inform the men of what circumstances are before them.
units.zh: 一堆尚在闷烧的火。按各式用途摆放的木棍和石头。一个立着的武器架，上面放满吹管。弯曲的刀刃。还有一只死去的幼狼，脖子上拴着绳索。看过这些迹象，你立刻把眼前的情势告诉弟兄们。

provenance.method: Independent complete-unit English/Chinese translation and review, including every displayed branch.

units.source: A litter of dead wolf pups. Their open-bellied mother is by them, a collar around her neck. There's a line of gore trailing away from the scene, some tiny footsteps in the grass.
units.zh: 一窝死去的幼狼。母狼倒在旁边，腹部被剖开，脖子上还戴着项圈。一道血肉痕迹延伸向远处，草丛里留着一些细小的脚印。

provenance.method: Independent complete-unit English/Chinese translation and review, including every displayed branch.

units.source: All you're hearing is that you are in goblin territory. You advise the men to keep a close eye on their surroundings, lest the tricky gits get the drop on you.
units.zh: 你听到的这些，只说明一件事：你们已踏入地精的领地。你提醒弟兄们密切留意周围，免得被那些狡猾的混蛋偷袭。

provenance.method: Independent complete-unit English/Chinese translation and review, including every displayed branch.

units.source: {#1}{#2}{#3/}{/#2}{/#1} {#4}Your arrival in {#5}Townname{/#5} seems to be cause for some celebration. One of the town's councilman greets you, offering refreshments.{/#4}
units.zh: {#1}{#2}{#3/}{/#2}{/#1} {#4}你来到{#5}这座城镇{/#5}，似乎成了值得庆祝的事。一位镇议员迎上来，招待你们吃喝。{/#4}

provenance.method: Independent complete-unit English/Chinese translation and review, including every displayed branch.

units.source: {#1}Townname{/#1} shows its appreciation for your business there by handing you and your men a tray of refreshments. {#2}Randombrother{/#2} slams a few mugs down as a dainty, girlish server looks on in awe. He wipes his mouth.
units.zh: {#1}这座城镇{/#1}为感谢你们在当地的生意，端来一托盘酒食，招待你和弟兄们。{#2}一名弟兄{/#2}接连灌下几大杯，一位娇小、女孩模样的侍者在旁看得目瞪口呆。他擦了擦嘴。

provenance.method: Independent complete-unit English/Chinese translation and review, including every displayed branch.

units.source: {#1}Business in {#2}Townname{/#2} has been good and the people there seem to appreciate you more and more: on today's arrival they gave you {#3}{#4}{#5}{#6/}{/#5}{/#4} {#7}plenty of useless thanks{/#7}{#8}a storm of gratitude{/#8}{#9}flowers upon flowers which you have no use for{/#9}{#10}trinkets and other things that you throw away when the peasants aren't looking{/#10}{#11}a tray of ale which your men quickly consume{/#11}{#12}a cask of ale which your men tactlessly criticize as 'tasting wooden'{/#12}{#13}a few marriage proposals which you gracefully turn down{/#13}{#14}a few marriage proposals which you can't turn down fast enough{/#14}{#15}one marriage proposal from the town ugly. She has a face that could stop a sundial. You decline the offer{/#15}{#16}a quick celebration wherein a few people shouted incoherently. Their tone seemed cheery, anyway{/#16}{#17}a few slaps on the back. You reminded them that such a doing might leave them handless on the next go around{/#17}{#18}an offering of orphans. You've no idea what gave them the notion that you'd accept such a gift, but you return the children to their sad home, also known as the streets{/#18}{/#3}.{/#1}
units.zh: {#1}在{#2}这座城镇{/#2}的生意一直不错，当地人似乎也越来越喜欢你们。今天抵达时，他们送上了{#3}{#4}{#5}{#6/}{/#5}{/#4} {#7}一大堆毫无用处的感谢{/#7}{#8}铺天盖地的谢意{/#8}{#9}一束又一束你们根本用不上的鲜花{/#9}{#10}小饰品和其他杂物，等农民们不留意时，你便把这些东西扔了{/#10}{#11}一托盘麦酒，弟兄们很快就喝光了{/#11}{#12}一桶麦酒，弟兄们却不识趣地抱怨“喝着有木头味”{/#12}{#13}几桩求婚，你礼貌地一一谢绝{/#13}{#14}几桩求婚，你恨不得立刻全部拒绝{/#14}{#15}镇上丑女的一次求婚。她那张脸丑得连日晷都能看停，你拒绝了{/#15}{#16}一场短暂的庆祝，几个人大喊着听不清的话，不过语气听起来倒是很高兴{/#16}{#17}几记热情的拍背。你提醒他们，下次再这么干，手可能就保不住了{/#17}{#18}一群孤儿。你完全不明白，他们怎么会觉得你会收下这种礼物，便把孩子们送回了他们可怜的家——也就是街头{/#18}{/#3}。{/#1}

The face of it is remarkably similar to your own, but you consider this nothing more than a coincidence.{/#16}{#17}a few rambunctious children, no doubt set loose by their parents to do evil that, in the adult world, would have garnered some measure of violent response. As the little runts go after you causing chaos, you order your men to put their boots to work. A few good stomps and kicks drive the bastards off, but for how long?{/#17}{#18}a burning effigy in your likeness. The peasants douse it in a pig trough. units.zh: {#10}这座城镇{/#10}的{#1}{#2}{#3}{#4/}{/#3}{/#2} {#5}居民{/#5}{#6}市民{/#6}{#7}农民{/#7}{#8}平民{/#8}{#9}镇民{/#9}{/#1}这样迎接你们：{#11}{#12}{#13}{#14/}{/#13}{/#12} {#15}几颗臭鸡蛋飞了过来，扔得又猛又准，让你不由得觉得，这些人似乎不太欢迎你们。{/#15}{#16}附近的树上吊着一个涂满焦油、粘着羽毛的人偶，正来回晃荡。那张脸和你惊人地相似，不过你只当是巧合。{/#16}{#17}几个闹腾的孩子冲了过来。毫无疑问，是他们的父母放任他们作恶，换成成年人干这些事，早就挨揍了。小崽子们追着你捣乱，你便命弟兄们动用靴子。几脚有力的踩踏和踢踹把这帮混小子赶跑了，可又能清静多久？{/#17}{#18}一个照着你模样扎的人像正在燃烧。农民们把它浸入猪食槽中灭火，又围成一圈，不让你看见那具像你的木像还剩什么。{/#18}{/#11}

units.source: {#1}{#2}{#3/}{/#2}{/#1} {#4}A cairn with an unusual skull atop it. Perhaps a memorial to a great orc warrior. No matter what it means to the greenskins, what it means to you is simple: you're in their territory now.{/#4}
units.zh: {#1}{#2}{#3/}{/#2}{/#1} {#4}一座石冢，顶上放着一颗奇特的头骨。也许是在纪念某位强大的兽人战士。不论这对绿皮意味着什么，对你来说，意思很简单：你们已经进入它们的领地。{/#4}

provenance.method: Independent complete-unit English/Chinese translation and review, including every displayed branch.

units.source: You come across a wooden totem with curvatures cut into it. {#1}Randombrother{/#1} believes that they are traces of the night sky, perhaps of this constellation or that.
units.zh: 你遇到一根木制图腾，上面刻着弯曲的线条。{#1}一名弟兄{/#1}认为，那是描绘夜空的图案，也许代表着某些星座。

provenance.method: Independent complete-unit English/Chinese translation and review, including every displayed branch.

units.source: {#1}Randombrother2{/#1} spits and says all it means is that you're in orc territory and you'd best pay better mind to that than what the lights in the night are doing.
units.zh: {#1}另一名弟兄{/#1}啐了一口，说这些只说明你们已踏入兽人的领地。比起夜里那些光点在做什么，最好多留意眼前的危险。

units.source: {#1}You find bones in the grass. The curvature of the ribs is obscene - far too large for a man. You wonder if it is that of a donkey, but the discovery of an enormous and oddly human-shaped skull confirms your suspicions: you've come onto orc territory.{/#1}
units.zh: {#1}你在草丛中发现了一些骨头。肋骨弯出的弧度大得离谱，绝不可能属于人类。你正猜测是不是驴骨，随后发现的一颗巨大头骨却证实了你的怀疑：那头骨形状竟有几分像人。你们已踏进兽人的领地。{/#1}

provenance.method: Independent complete-unit English/Chinese translation and review, including every displayed branch.

units.source: Human heads on spikes. Their bodies - limbless - clumped into piles. They've been cut and mutilated. The only sense of humanity they have left are the shreds of clothes barely clinging to their destroyed flesh.
units.zh: 人头插在尖桩上。失去四肢的尸身堆成一堆，刀痕遍布，残缺不全。勉强挂在破碎血肉上的衣物碎片，是它们曾为人的最后一点痕迹。

provenance.method: Independent complete-unit English/Chinese translation and review, including every displayed branch.

units.source: You come across a man's body, but not his head. That's gone. His genitals are also gone. And his feet and hands. Javelins stick out of what's left, someone or something have turned what remains into gruesome target practice.
units.zh: 你遇到一具男人的尸体，却没见到他的脑袋。脑袋不见了，生殖器也不见了，双手双脚同样不见。剩下的残躯上插着标枪，有人，或者什么东西，把它当成了骇人的练习靶。

units.source: You find a shattered skeleton nailed to a tree by an enormous axe. It's mostly just the chest cavity for the rest of it has long since fallen apart. Long, curving artwork has been carved into the tree trunk.
units.zh: 你发现一副破碎的骨架，被一把巨斧钉在树上。基本只剩下胸廓，其余部分早已散落。树干上刻着修长、弯曲的图案。

provenance.method: Independent complete-unit English/Chinese translation and review, including every displayed branch.

units.source: You come to a stack of stones carefully placed on a small hillside. Inspecting them, you find white carvings on the rocks. Each one displays a different story - ones where large brutes wander and cause disturbing amounts of violence toward smaller, thinner stick figures. {#1}Randombrother{/#1} laughs at the drawings.
units.zh: 你来到一座小山坡前，上面有一堆精心摆放的石头。仔细看去，石面上有白色的刻画。每块石头都讲述着不同的故事：高大的蛮横家伙四处游荡，对那些更矮、更瘦的简笔小人施以令人不安的暴力。{#1}一名弟兄{/#1}看着这些画，笑了起来。

provenance.method: Independent complete-unit English/Chinese translation and review, including every displayed branch.

units.source: A leather tarp is found flapping from some sticks on a hill. There's evidence of an abandoned camp around it - a smoldering fire, fleeting footprints, a few bits of odd debris. {#1}Randombrother{/#1} points at it all.
units.zh: 山坡上，几根木棍撑着一块皮篷，正随风拍动。周围留着营地废弃的迹象：闷烧的火堆、逐渐模糊的脚印，还有几块古怪的碎屑。{#1}一名弟兄{/#1}指着这一切。

provenance.method: Independent complete-unit English/Chinese translation and review, including every displayed branch.

units.source: {#1}Randombrother{/#1} walks up to a stack of human skulls you've come across. He analyzes their mortal wounds - mostly the fact that their bodies are nowhere in sight, decapitation is a hell of a thing to survive. Standing back up, he nods.
units.zh: {#1}一名弟兄{/#1}走到你们发现的一堆人头骨前。他分析起它们的致命伤——主要依据是附近根本看不到尸身，毕竟丢了脑袋还能活可不容易。他站起身，点了点头。

provenance.method: Independent complete-unit English/Chinese translation and review, including every displayed branch.

units.source: You also nod and tell the men to be aware of the dangers ahead.
units.zh: 你也点点头，叫弟兄们留意前方的危险。

provenance.method: Independent complete-unit English/Chinese translation and review, including every displayed branch.

units.source: {#1}There's a feeling to the wilderness and there's a feeling to civilization - and what you got here doesn't fit either. You got an odd sensation as though you'd just trespassed unto someone else's territory. A gruesome pile of dead bodies shorn of any humanity they once had also helps make the distinction, and settle the simple matter of fact that you have now entered orcish lands.{/#1}
units.zh: {#1}荒野有荒野的感觉，文明之地也有自己的感觉，可这里两者都不像。你有种奇怪的感受，仿佛刚刚擅自闯入了别人的地盘。一堆惨不忍睹、已被剥去一切人样的尸体，也帮你分清了这一点，并确定了一个简单的事实：你们已经进入兽人的土地。{/#1}

units.source: Upon hearing some sellswords yelling at each other, you reluctantly set aside your quill pen and step outside your tent. There you find {#1}Hauntedbrother1{/#1} and {#2}Hauntedbrother2{/#2} in each other's faces - and between them they're pulling at the Grand Diviner's flail. What is being screamed between them are obscenities of a most graphic nature, and just as you're about to step in the flail glows a bright green and both sellswords drop the weapon to lunge at each other. The fight is ended fast, but not without injuries.
units.zh: 听见几个佣兵互相吼叫，你不情愿地放下羽毛笔，走出帐篷。你看见{#1}受影响的弟兄甲{/#1}和{#2}受影响的弟兄乙{/#2}正脸对脸地争执，两人之间拉扯着大先知的连枷。他们对骂的话污秽露骨至极。正当你准备上前制止，连枷突然亮起耀眼的绿光，两名佣兵丢下武器，扑向彼此。打斗很快被制止，但还是有人受了伤。

provenance.method: Independent complete-unit English/Chinese translation and review, including every displayed branch.

units.source: You dream of your mother. You had not seen her face in some time, and thought you'd forgotten it, the world having ground down most memories. She is as lovely as you'd expect, and she draws you in, hand about your hair, threading her fingers through it, the soft hiss of her touch met by the gentlest of whispers. And a moment later she offers a breast to you, and you reel back, unsure, and when you look up the Grand Diviner is there, grinning madly.
units.zh: 你梦见了母亲。你已许久没见过她的脸，还以为自己早已忘记，毕竟这世界磨灭了太多回忆。她一如你记忆中那般温柔美丽，拉你靠近，手拢着你的头发，指间穿过发丝，轻柔的摩挲声伴着最温和的低语。片刻后，她把一只乳房凑向你。你迟疑地向后退缩，抬头看时，眼前却成了大先知，正疯狂地咧嘴笑着。

provenance.method: Independent complete-unit English/Chinese translation and review, including every displayed branch.

units.source: With a snarl, you rip out of the dream and flip off your cot and hit the ground, gasping for air and slapping your face as if whatever dreamt of came back with you. The rest of the company is in an equal state of disrepair, every sellsword having been struck by the same nightmare. You glance over to inventory to see the Grand Diviner's flail bristling a bright green, then it fades from your stare, the slightest chuckle following it out...
units.zh: 你怒吼着挣脱梦境，翻下行军床摔到地上，大口喘气，不停拍打自己的脸，仿佛梦里的东西也跟着你回来了。战团其他人同样狼狈不堪，每个佣兵都遭遇了同一个噩梦。你朝行李那边望去，只见大先知的连枷正迸着亮绿的光。那光在你的注视下渐渐退去，末了还跟着一声极轻的窃笑……

provenance.method: Independent complete-unit English/Chinese translation and review, including every displayed branch.

units.source: {#1}Hauntedbrother{/#1} spills into your tent yelling that you did terrible things to him while he was sleeping. You stand and draw your sword, for the details of his accusations are certainly worth killing another man over, but as you both pause to breathe, you realize {#2}Hauntedbrother{/#2} has the Grand Diviner's flail firmly grasped in a whiteknuckled hand. The green mist swirling in its center brims bright, then fades as you both look at it. The sellsword throws it to the ground.
units.zh: {#1}受惊的弟兄{/#1}跌跌撞撞地冲进帐篷，大喊你趁他睡着时对他做了可怕的事。你站起身拔出剑，因为他指控的那些细节，足以让人拔剑杀人。可当你们都停下来喘气时，你注意到{#2}这名弟兄{/#2}正死死握着大先知的连枷，指节都攥白了。连枷中央旋转的绿雾亮了起来，又在你们一同注视时暗了下去。佣兵把它扔在地上。

provenance.method: Independent complete-unit English/Chinese translation and review, including every displayed branch.

units.source: But it took so much to get it... (the event ends)
units.zh: 可我们费了那么大劲才弄到它……（事件结束）

units.source: You find {#1}Hauntedbrother{/#1} staring into the Grand Diviner's flail. The glassy bulb is filled with mist, and the sellsword is raking his tongue to suck up the condensation. Hand to your sword, you ask what he's doing, and the man freezes, and his eyes open and he jerks back like a man snorting awake knowing he's late for work.
units.zh: 你发现{#1}这名弟兄{/#1}正盯着大先知的连枷。玻璃球里满是雾气，佣兵竟伸着舌头舔舐，吸吮凝结的水珠。你把手按在剑上，问他在做什么。那人僵住了，睁开眼，猛地向后一缩，活像一个惊醒后才发现自己上工迟到的人。

units.source: Some of the men have said the weapon has been murmuring when nobody's looking, and it seems every so often it does capture someone's ear...
units.zh: 有些弟兄说，这件武器总会趁没人注意时低声呢喃，看来它时不时还真能勾住某个人的耳朵……

units.source: It's only a weapon, you fools. (the event ends)
units.zh: 不过是件武器，你们这些蠢货。（事件结束）

units.source: A voice seeps into the darkness: wherever she is... your mother knows she abandoned you... wherever I am... you know I would love you as greatly as her absence has harmed you. I will mother you to power, sellsword, I will feed you the milk of life from...
units.zh: 一个声音渗入黑暗：无论她身在何方……你母亲都知道，她抛弃了你……无论我身在何方……你都知道，她的缺席伤你有多深，我就会给你多深的爱。我会像母亲一样哺育你，让你变得强大，佣兵，我会用生命的乳汁喂养你，从……

units.source: You stare at the flail, watching as the viridian glow shimmers and then dims, a grotesque chuckling echoing as it fades.
units.zh: 你盯着连枷，看着翠绿的光芒闪烁、黯淡，一阵怪诞的窃笑随着光芒消退而回荡。
